review_basis.area: Reference command, revisions and stopping behavior
review_basis.evidence: Current peer TOML agrees with the documented exact config path, two clients, one round, one epoch, CPU FP32 command, serial client training, batch size 1, max_length 64, AdamW rate and LoRA targets/rank/alpha/dropout. Current null target_perplexity setting enables the perplexity label without a threshold stop; the later CLI log reports perplexity 131.47 and explicitly stops at its one-round budget. Artifact identity helper agrees with the same-repository revision inheritance and independent tokenizer default-main descriptions.

The directly read qualification.json hash and contents exactly match the documentation author's receipt. Guide correctly distinguishes tiny offline architecture tests, actual pinned pretrained qualification, and plato.py socket/process launch. 14.87 seconds and 4258660352 bytes/about 3.97 GiB are stated only for one shared-base qualification process with serial logical clients of sizes 2 and 3. It reports frozen base, adapter update/weighted aggregation/reload checks and finite held-out perplexity without a benchmark/convergence claim. The original source/receipt makes no false claim that the normal CLI had passed at authoring time.

Current trainer exports PEFT adapters through save_pretrained with embedding export disabled for q_proj/v_proj, writes the adapter tree in Plato's safetensors checkpoint, and writes .hf JSON artifact identity/config plus .pkl run-history sidecar. Load restores via set_peft_model_state_dict into the wrapper, checks identity/key/shape, and retains the base. Guide correctly says this is adapter checkpoint/reload and does not imply full optimizer-state resume.
